node.statement: Because sum_l w_k(l)=0 and t=max(t,0)-max(-t,0) for each real t, summing over the coordinates of w_k gives sum_l max(w_k(l),0)=sum_l max(-w_k(l),0)=n(w_k). Substituting this into 1.4.1.3 gives n(w_i-w_k)<=n(w_i)+n(w_k); since i was arbitrary, this proves 1.4.1 without using node 1.3.
